claims.text: The National Military Command Center recorded the penetration at command level. Its Memorandum for Record of 29 October 1975, 0605 EST, subject 'AFB Penetration', signed C. D. Roberts, Jr., Brigadier General, USMC, Deputy Director for Operations, states: 'At 290200 EST AFOC informed NMCC that an unidentified helicopter, possibly two, had been sighted flying low over Loring AFB Maine, in proximity to a weapons storage area.'

claims.source: NMCC DDO update as of 292200 EST Oct 75, citing 42 BW CP LORING AFB 291140Z OCT 75 and SAC CP OPS CONTROL 291954Z OCT 75, http://www.nicap.org/reports/751027loring_1-6.htm , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The escalation reached the Army Staff and the State Department. The DDO update as of 292200 EST records that the Chief of Staff of the Air Force operations division requested the Army National Guard helicopter be provided until 300800 EST 'to track and identify the intruder; no apprehension to take place; the Canadian Border would not be crossed', that the request was under consideration by the Department of the Army Director of Operations, DCSOPS, that a military aide to the Special Assistant to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense had been advised, and that 'The State Department Canadian Desk Officer has been kept informed.'

claims.source: NICAP, 'UFOs Intrude Into SAC Base Weapons Areas', http://www.nicap.org/intsac.htm , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: A teletype message to the National Military Command Center states: 'The A/C definitely penetrated the LAFB northern perimeter and on one occasion was within 300 yards of the munitions storage area perimeter.'

claims.text: A Loring operations report records: 'It is our opinion that the unknown helicopter has demonstrated a clear intent in the weapons storage area, is smart and a most capable aviator.' This is the phrase from which Fawcett and Greenwood took the title of their 1984 book.

desc: THE HUB WHERE THE BEST DOCUMENT IN THE SUBJECT WAS GENERATED. Loring Air Force Base at Limestone, Maine was a Strategic Air Command installation home to the 42nd Bombardment Wing and a nuclear weapons storage area, and on the nights of 27, 28 and 29 to 30 October 1975 that storage area was overflown at low level by something the United States military tracked, pursued and failed to identify. What makes Loring the strongest node in this cluster is not the sighting reports but the paper trail above them. The National Military Command Center produced a Memorandum for Record over the signature of a serving brigadier general with a subject line reading 'AFB Penetration', distributed to the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, the Director of the Joint Staff, the J-30 through J-38 directorates, the service chiefs, and the DIA, NSA and CIA representatives. A Major General of the Army Staff personally approved rules of engagement for a National Guard helicopter: track and identify, no apprehension, no border crossing. The State Department's Canadian desk officer was kept informed. Nothing in this record says what the object was, and the traffic calls it an unidentified helicopter throughout rather than a UFO. What it documents is a three-day command-level flap over an unidentified rotary-wing intruder at a nuclear weapons storage area, escalated to the Joint Staff and to a foreign government, which is a nuclear security record before it is anything else.

unverified: The 42nd Bombardment Wing unit history for October to December 1975, held at the Air Force Historical Research Agency, has not been sought or opened. The Wurtsmith precedent makes its contents genuinely unpredictable: there, the wing historian checked his own Oct-Dec 1975 history and found no reference to the incident at all.

An OSI teletype of 29 October 1975 and an OSI letter of 21 April 1977 titled 'Overflight of USAF Installations by Unidentified Aircraft' are cited by NICAP from Clear Intent and were NOT OPENED in their own text by this board.
The base's own institutional history, dates of operation and closure are not asserted here because no source establishing them was opened by this pass.
